# codx-junior — demo deployment

One container, one command, one API key.

```bash
cd codx-junior-installer/demo
./up.sh --provider deepseek --key sk-xxxxxxxxxxxx
# -> http://localhost:19981
```

This is the **tier 1** deployment: what you give somebody who wants to try
codx-junior. It is pull-only (nothing is compiled on their machine), it does not
run Milvus, Traefik, LocalAI, a second API container, an init container or a
Node server, and restarting it installs nothing.

| | Full deployment (`codx-junior/docker-compose.yaml`) | Demo (this folder) |
|---|---|---|
| Containers | 8 | **1** (+1 optional) |
| Image size | several GB | **~1 GB** |
| First start | build + `pip install torch/vLLM` + `npm i` | **pull + 30 s** |
| Install steps at boot | `chown -R $HOME`, `uv sync` | **none** |
| Ports to publish | 80, 443 (+ routing) | **19981** |
| Needs a domain / TLS | yes (Traefik + ACME) | **no** |
| What you must configure | domain, ACME, LiteLLM keys, Milvus, LocalAI models | **one provider + one key** |

---

## 1. What you must pass

Only two settings are mandatory. Everything else has a working default.

| Setting | Required | Example | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER` | **yes** | `deepseek` | Which OpenAI-compatible provider to use |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY` | **yes** | `sk-…` | Key of that provider |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL` | only for `custom` | `https://gw.acme.com/v1` | Override the preset endpoint |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL` | no | `deepseek-chat` | Override the preset chat model |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH` | no | `~/my-projects` | Host folder with your repositories (default `./projects`) |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_WEB_PORT` | no | `8080` | Web UI port (default `19981`) |

You can pass them on the command line (`./up.sh --provider … --key …`), or write
them in `.env` (copy `.env.example`), or export them in your shell.

### Provider presets

`CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER` selects a preset; codx-junior fills in the base URL,
the chat model, the wiki model and the embeddings model for you.

| Provider | Base URL used | Default chat model | Embeddings model | Get a key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `openai` | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | `gpt-4.1-mini` (`gpt-4.1` for wiki) | `text-embedding-3-small` (1536) | platform.openai.com/api-keys |
| `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com/v1` | `deepseek-chat` | *none* → RAG disabled | platform.deepseek.com/api_keys |
| `gemini` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai` | `gemini-2.0-flash` | `text-embedding-004` (768) | aistudio.google.com/app/apikey |
| `openrouter` | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `openai/gpt-4o-mini` | *none* → RAG disabled | openrouter.ai/keys |
| `mistral` | `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` | `mistral-large-latest` | `mistral-embed` (1024) | console.mistral.ai/api-keys |
| `groq` | `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` | `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` | *none* → RAG disabled | console.groq.com/keys |
| `ollama` | `http://localhost:11434/v1` | `llama3.1` | `nomic-embed-text` (768) | local, no key |
| `custom` | `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL` | `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL` | `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_EMBEDDINGS_MODEL` | — |

Notes:

* **Everything goes through the `openai` client.** Any gateway exposing
  `/chat/completions` + `/embeddings` with a `/v1` path works as `custom`
  (LiteLLM, Portkey, vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio, Azure OpenAI proxy…).
* **Anthropic** has no OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Run LiteLLM in front of it
  and use `--provider custom --url http://litellm:4000/v1`.
* Providers without an embeddings endpoint keep **knowledge/RAG search disabled**
  (the rest of the app works). Add an embeddings model later from *Global
  settings → AI models*.

---

## 2. What codx-junior configures by itself

On the first start the API reads the settings above and, **only if no provider
has been configured yet**, it:

1. creates the `AIProvider` (name = the provider you chose) with its base URL
   and key;
2. creates the models `knowledge` (chat/coding/RAG/guardrail) and `embeddings`
   (plus a `wiki` entry when the preset uses a different model for the wiki);
3. points the five global model slots (`llm_model`, `rag_model`, `wiki_model`,
   `guardrail_model`, `embeddings_model`) at them;
4. writes a summary to `$CODX_JUNIOR_CONFIG_FOLDER/bootstrap.json`.

Result: you open the UI, pick a project, and the chat works. No settings page,
no model import, no "no model configured" dead end.

It is **idempotent and non-destructive**: an installation already configured
from the UI is never touched. To re-apply (e.g. after rotating a key):

```bash
./up.sh --keep          # or:
docker exec codx-junior curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19980/api/bootstrap/apply
docker exec codx-junior curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19980/api/bootstrap   # inspect
```

`CODX_JUNIOR_AI_FORCE=1` makes every start re-apply it;
`CODX_JUNIOR_AI_BOOTSTRAP=0` disables it entirely.

The key itself is **not** written to the settings files: the provider stores
`$CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY` and it is expanded from the environment at use time
(`global_settings.get_provider_settings`).

---

## 3. What this deployment leaves out

| Component of the full stack | Why it is not here | How to get it back |
|---|---|---|
| **client** container (Node + `vite preview`) | the SPA is compiled in a builder stage and served by nginx | never needed |
| **api-background** container | runs as a supervisord program in the same container | never needed |
| **traefik** | same-origin: nginx proxies `/api` to the API | add a proxy in front, or use the server tier |
| **localai** | replaced by "bring your own provider key" | `codx-junior/docker-compose.yaml` |
| **milvus** | only vector backend, but heavy (~1 GB RAM) | `./up.sh --knowledge` |
| **analytics-init / codx-junior-init** | their `mkdir`/`chown` work is done by the entrypoint | — |
| torch / sentence-transformers / vLLM / Playwright / TeX / Tesseract / Firefox | runtime deps of optional features; now `pip` extras (`.[local-models,browser]`) | full deployment installs them |

Features **not available** in the demo without extra work: local (offline)
embeddings, document → PDF/DOCX conversion, Tesseract OCR, browser/computer
sessions and workspaces (they need `/var/run/docker.sock`), knowledge/RAG search
(needs `--knowledge`).

To enable the docker-dependent features, uncomment the socket mount in
`docker-compose.yaml`. Be aware that it gives the container control of the host
Docker daemon.

---

## 4. Operating it

```bash
./up.sh                      # start (idempotent)
./up.sh --knowledge          # also start Milvus
./up.sh --build              # build the image from source instead of pulling
docker compose logs -f codx-junior
docker compose down          # stop (volumes are kept)
docker compose down -v       # stop and delete settings/analytics
```

Ports and volumes:

| | |
|---|---|
| `19981` | Web UI (published) |
| `19980` | API (internal, proxied by nginx) |
| volume `codx-junior-settings` | global settings, per-project `.codx`, presets |
| volume `codx-junior-analytics` | token usage, AI logs, API metrics |
| bind `${CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH}` | your repositories |

The health check is `GET /api/health`. `docker compose ps` shows `healthy` when
the API answers.

---

## 5. Development deployment (unchanged)

The watch/reload deployment is still `codx-junior/docker-compose.yaml` +
`codx-junior/docker-compose.build.yaml` (+ `docker-compose.dev.yaml`): it mounts
the source tree over the image, sets `DEBUG=1`, runs Vite dev server with HMR,
and `scripts/run_api.sh` syncs the environment on start. Use it when you hack on

# codx-junior — demo deployment

One container, one command, one API key.

```bash
cd codx-junior-installer/demo
./up.sh --provider deepseek --key sk-xxxxxxxxxxxx
# -> http://localhost:19981
```

This is the **tier 1** deployment: what you give somebody who wants to try
codx-junior. It is pull-only (nothing is compiled on their machine), it does not
run Milvus, Traefik, LocalAI, a second API container, an init container or a
Node server, and restarting it installs nothing.

| | Full deployment (`codx-junior/docker-compose.yaml`) | Demo (this folder) |
|---|---|---|
| Containers | 8 | **1** (+1 optional) |
| Image size | several GB | **~1 GB** |
| First start | build + `pip install torch/vLLM` + `npm i` | **pull + 30 s** |
| Install steps at boot | `chown -R $HOME`, `uv sync` | **none** |
| Ports to publish | 80, 443 (+ routing) | **19981** |
| Needs a domain / TLS | yes (Traefik + ACME) | **no** |
| What you must configure | domain, ACME, LiteLLM keys, Milvus, LocalAI models | **one provider + one key** |

---

## 1. What you must pass

Only two settings are mandatory. Everything else has a working default.

| Setting | Required | Example | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER` | **yes** | `deepseek` | Which OpenAI-compatible provider to use |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY` | **yes** | `sk-…` | Key of that provider |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL` | only for `custom` | `https://gw.acme.com/v1` | Override the preset endpoint |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL` | no | `deepseek-chat` | Override the preset chat model |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH` | no | `~/my-projects` | Host folder with your repositories (default `./projects`) |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_WEB_PORT` | no | `8080` | Web UI port (default `19981`) |

You can pass them on the command line (`./up.sh --provider … --key …`), or write
them in `.env` (copy `.env.example`), or export them in your shell.

### Provider presets

`CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER` selects a preset; codx-junior fills in the base URL,
the chat model, the wiki model and the embeddings model for you.

| Provider | Base URL used | Default chat model | Embeddings model | Get a key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `openai` | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | `gpt-4.1-mini` (`gpt-4.1` for wiki) | `text-embedding-3-small` (1536) | platform.openai.com/api-keys |
| `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com/v1` | `deepseek-chat` | *none* → RAG disabled | platform.deepseek.com/api_keys |
| `gemini` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai` | `gemini-2.0-flash` | `text-embedding-004` (768) | aistudio.google.com/app/apikey |
| `openrouter` | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `openai/gpt-4o-mini` | *none* → RAG disabled | openrouter.ai/keys |
| `mistral` | `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` | `mistral-large-latest` | `mistral-embed` (1024) | console.mistral.ai/api-keys |
| `groq` | `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` | `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` | *none* → RAG disabled | console.groq.com/keys |
| `ollama` | `http://localhost:11434/v1` | `llama3.1` | `nomic-embed-text` (768) | local, no key |
| `custom` | `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL` | `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL` | `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_EMBEDDINGS_MODEL` | — |

Notes:

* **Everything goes through the `openai` client.** Any gateway exposing
  `/chat/completions` + `/embeddings` with a `/v1` path works as `custom`
  (LiteLLM, Portkey, vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio, Azure OpenAI proxy…).
* **Anthropic** has no OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Run LiteLLM in front of it
  and use `--provider custom --url http://litellm:4000/v1`.
* Providers without an embeddings endpoint keep **knowledge/RAG search disabled**
  (the rest of the app works). Add an embeddings model later from *Global
  settings → AI models*.

---

## 2. What codx-junior configures by itself

On the first start the API reads the settings above and, **only if no provider
has been configured yet**, it:

1. creates the `AIProvider` (name = the provider you chose) with its base URL
   and key;
2. creates the models `knowledge` (chat/coding/RAG/guardrail) and `embeddings`
   (plus a `wiki` entry when the preset uses a different model for the wiki);
3. points the five global model slots (`llm_model`, `rag_model`, `wiki_model`,
   `guardrail_model`, `embeddings_model`) at them;
4. writes a summary to `$CODX_JUNIOR_CONFIG_FOLDER/bootstrap.json`.

Result: you open the UI, pick a project, and the chat works. No settings page,
no model import, no "no model configured" dead end.

It is **idempotent and non-destructive**: an installation already configured
from the UI is never touched. To re-apply (e.g. after rotating a key):

```bash
docker exec codx-junior curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19980/api/bootstrap/apply
docker exec codx-junior curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19980/api/bootstrap   # inspect
```

`CODX_JUNIOR_AI_FORCE=1` makes every start re-apply it;
`CODX_JUNIOR_AI_BOOTSTRAP=0` disables it entirely.

The key itself is **not** written to the settings files: the provider stores
`$CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY` and it is expanded from the environment at use time
(`global_settings.get_provider_settings`).

---

## 3. What this deployment leaves out

| Component of the full stack | Why it is not here | How to get it back |
|---|---|---|
| **client** container (Node + `vite preview`) | the SPA is compiled in a builder stage and served by nginx | never needed |
| **api-background** container | runs as a supervisord program in the same container | never needed |
| **traefik** | same-origin: nginx proxies `/api` to the API | add a proxy in front, or use the server tier |
| **localai** | replaced by "bring your own provider key" | `codx-junior/docker-compose.yaml` |
| **milvus** | only vector backend, but heavy (~1 GB RAM) | `./up.sh --knowledge` |
| **analytics-init / codx-junior-init** | their `mkdir`/`chown` work is done by the entrypoint | — |
| torch / sentence-transformers / vLLM / Playwright / TeX / Tesseract / Firefox | runtime deps of optional features; now `pip` extras (`.[local-models,browser]`) | full deployment installs them |

Features **not available** in the demo without extra work: local (offline)
embeddings, document → PDF/DOCX conversion, Tesseract OCR, browser/computer
sessions and workspaces (they need `/var/run/docker.sock`), knowledge/RAG search
(needs `--knowledge`).

To enable the docker-dependent features, uncomment the socket mount in
`docker-compose.yaml`. Be aware that it gives the container control of the host
Docker daemon.

---

## 4. Operating it

```bash
./up.sh                      # start (idempotent)
./up.sh --knowledge          # also start Milvus
./up.sh --build              # build the image from source instead of pulling
docker compose logs -f codx-junior
docker compose down          # stop (volumes are kept)
docker compose down -v       # stop and delete settings/analytics
```

Ports and volumes:

| | |
|---|---|
| `19981` | Web UI (published) |
| `19980` | API (internal, proxied by nginx) |
| volume `codx-junior-settings` | global settings, per-project `.codx`, presets |
| volume `codx-junior-analytics` | token usage, AI logs, API metrics |
| bind `${CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH}` | your repositories |

The health check is `GET /api/health`. `docker compose ps` shows `healthy` when
the API answers.

---

## 5. Development deployment (unchanged)

The watch/reload deployment is still `codx-junior/docker-compose.yaml` +
`codx-junior/docker-compose.build.yaml` (+ `docker-compose.dev.yaml`): it mounts
the source tree over the image, sets `DEBUG=1`, runs Vite dev server with HMR,

  `scripts/run_api.sh` runs on every start.
* `CODX_JUNIOR_API_EXTRAS` — extras installed by `scripts/install_api.sh`
  (default `local-models,browser`, empty for a slim install).

| `401` / `invalid api key` in the logs | wrong key, or `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL` missing `/v1`. |

```md codx-junior-installer/FAST-DEPLOYMENT.md
# Fast deployment analysis — codx-junior

Status: analysis + proposal (nothing in this document has been implemented yet).
Scope: `codx-junior-installer/codx-junior/*`, `scripts/install_*.sh`, `scripts/run_*.sh`,
`api/pyproject.toml`.

Goal: make `codx-junior` **cheap to build, cheap to pull and one command to run**, so
people can try it in minutes instead of waiting for a multi-gigabyte build.

---

## 1. What we deploy today

`codx-junior-installer/codx-junior/docker-compose.yaml` starts **8 services**
(2 of them one-shot init containers):

| # | Service | Image | Why it is there | Verdict |
|---|---------|-------|-----------------|---------|
| 1 | `codx-junior-api` | `codxjunior/codx-junior:api` (built) | FastAPI, `shm_size: 4gb`, mounts host `docker.sock`, mounts the **source tree** over the image | keep (slim) |
| 2 | `codx-junior-api-background` | same image | second full Python stack (`CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND=1`), `shm_size: 4gb` | collapse into #1 |
| 3 | `codx-junior-client` | `codxjunior/codx-junior:client` (built) | Node + nvm + `node_modules`, runs `npm run preview` | replace |
| 4 | `milvus-codx-junior` | `milvusdb/milvus:v2.5.11` | vector store for knowledge/RAG (embedded etcd) | keep (only backend in code) |
| 5 | `localai-codx-junior` | built `FROM localai/localai:latest` | "optional local models", but started by default, `shm_size: 20gb` | move to a profile |
| 6 | `traefik-codx-junior` | `traefik:latest` | TLS + `forwardAuth` + workspace routing, ports 80/443, `docker.sock:ro`, ACME | move to a profile |
| 7 | `codx-junior-analytics-init` | `codxjunior/codx-junior:debian` | one-shot `mkdir` + `chown` of a volume | delete |
| 8 | `codx-junior-init` | `codxjunior/codx-junior:debian` | one-shot `initial-setup.sh`, `depends_on: localai` | delete |

The stack is wrapped again in `codx-junior-dind` (dockerd inside a container,
`runtime: sysbox-runc`), which re-runs the whole compose on boot and can
optionally download and install the **Coolify** stack (`coolify-install.sh`).

### What actually makes it slow and heavy

1. **Python dependency set is far bigger than the code needs.**
   `api/pyproject.toml` declares `vllm>=0.5.0`, `torch>=2.4.0`,
   `sentence-transformers>=6.2.0` and `playwright` as mandatory dependencies.
   * `codx/junior/ai/vllm_cpu_ai.py` is literally headed `## DEPRECATED: Using vllm docker openai compatible`.
   * `sentence_transformers` is imported **lazily** with a friendly `ImportError`
     (`knowledge/embeddings.py:80-86`).
   * No `import torch` exists anywhere in the API.
   These packages are installed on every build (`install_api.sh`
   → `uv pip install -e . --extra-index-url https://pytorch.org`) and are the
   single biggest contributor to image size and build time.
2. **OS package set is far bigger than the code needs.**
   `debian/Dockerfile.debian` installs `texlive-xetex` + `texlive-fonts-recommended`;
   the monolithic `codx-junior/Dockerfile` installs the whole `texlive` metapackage,
   plus `firefox-esr`, `tesseract-ocr`, `pandoc`, `fuse3`, `fuse-overlayfs`.
   TeX Live alone is commonly 1.5–2 GB compressed-to-layered. PDF/OCR conversion is
   a per-project, on-demand feature (`doc_converter`, `explain_image`), not a
   requirement to read a chat.
3. **The web client is built inside the runtime image.**
   `scripts/install_client.sh` does `rm -rf node_modules`, `nvm install v24.12.0`,
   `npm i`, `npm run build-only`. No layer caching (the `COPY`s run first), Node is
   re-downloaded on every build, and the final image keeps the full toolchain plus
   `node_modules` even though the container only runs `npm run preview`.
4. **`run_api.sh` installs at runtime.** On every container start it runs
   `sudo chown -R $HOME`, and `uv sync` (unlocked resolution, network) — and if the
   venv is missing it calls `install_api.sh`, i.e. a **cold container installs torch
   and vllm while the user waits**. `api/uv.lock` exists but is not used.
5. **No root `.dockerignore`.** The build context is the repository root
   (`context: ../..`), so `client/node_modules`, `.codx/`, `wiki/`,
   `docs/node_modules`, `design/`, `.git` are shipped to the daemon on every build.
6. **Duplicated layers in the monolithic Dockerfile.** `base` copies
   `client/ api/ scripts/ codx-junior/ …`, then the next stage copies them all
   again; two full copies end up in the image.
7. **Two uvicorn stacks × 8 workers.** `run_api.sh` defaults to
   `--workers ${WEB_CONCURRENCY:-8}`; the API and the background worker are
   separate containers with separate 4 GB `shm`, so a default install holds up to
   16 Python workers, each importing langchain/llama-index.
8. **Production compose mounts the source tree** (`../../.:/home/codx-junior/codx-junior`),
   which forces the dev layout on every install and shadows the image content.

Estimated effect (order of magnitude, to be measured): image pull ~6–9 GB and a
first build of tens of minutes, versus ~0.6–1.2 GB and a few minutes for the slim
path; idle RAM from several GB down to well under 2 GB.

---

## 2. Do we need all the services?

| Service | Needed to try the product? | Lighter alternative |
|---|---|---|
| API | yes | slim image, one process tree |
| API background worker | yes (indexing, orchestration worker) | run it as a `supervisor.conf` program **inside the API container** — `supervisor.conf` already defines `codx-junior-api`, `codx-junior-api-background` and `codx-junior-client` |
| Client | yes (the UI) | **static build** (multi-stage `node` builder) served by `nginx:alpine` (~10 MB) *or* by FastAPI `StaticFiles` → 0 extra containers |
| Milvus | needed for knowledge only | keep for trial; the real win is making the API **start without a reachable Milvus** so a first-time user can skip RAG. `sqlite-vec`/`LanceDB` would remove the container entirely but needs a new `KnowledgeDB` backend (medium effort, later) |
| Traefik | no for a trial (`localhost:19981` is enough) | profile `proxy`: needed only for TLS, custom domains and workspace routing |
| LocalAI | no | profile `local-models`; users bring OpenAI / Ollama / vLLM |
| analytics-init | no | create the volume in the entrypoint (`mkdir -p` + `chown` before dropping privileges) or use a bind mount prepared by the installer |
| codx-junior-init | no | fold into the API entrypoint / remove `depends_on: localai` |
| DIND wrapper | only for the hosted/"one VM per customer" product | keep as a separate deliverable, not on the trial path |
| Coolify | no | it is already opt-in (`COOLIFY_ENABLED`), keep it out of the default image |

## 3. Target: three tiers, one command each

### Tier 1 — Trial (super simple, what we advertise)

```sh
docker run -d --name codx-junior -p 19981:19981 \
  -v "$HOME/codx-projects:/home/codx-junior-projects" \
  -v codx-junior:/data \
  -e CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN=localhost \
  codxjunior/codx-junior:latest
```

* one pulled image, no build, no clone, no `.env`, no DNS, no certificate
* `supervisor` starts API + background worker + static client inside it
* knowledge is optional: if no `CODX_JUNIOR_MILVUS_URL` (or no reachable Milvus)
  the API runs in "no-knowledge" mode and the UI hides RAG features
* the user then only needs one API key (`Settings → AI Models`) plus a project folder

### Tier 2 — Local compose (developers / self-host, no TLS)

api (+ worker in-process) + optional `milvus` service, published ports, no Traefik,
no LocalAI, no client container, no init containers. `docker compose up -d` on a
repo checkout, ready in minutes.

### Tier 3 — Server (full, current behaviour)

Tier 2 **plus** `--profile proxy` (Traefik: TLS, `forwardAuth`, workspace routes),
`--profile local-models` (LocalAI/Ollama), workspaces and DIND. Same compose file,
opt-in profiles instead of a second file to maintain.

## 6. Review answers (three open points)

### 6.1 Are sqlite-vec / LanceDB equal to Milvus?

What the code actually uses (`api/codx/junior/knowledge/knowledge_db.py`):

| Capability used today | Where | Milvus | LanceDB | sqlite-vec |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Public surface callers need | `:272-280` (`index_documents`, `delete_documents`, `search`, `search_sparse`, `search_vector`, `search_hybrid`, `raw_search`, `get_all_sources`, `get_all_categoties`) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (hand-written) |
| BM25 lexical leg | `Function(name="text_bm25_emb", …)` `:419` | ✅ built-in | ✅ native FTS (Tantivy) | ⚠️ FTS5, different tokenizer |
| Dense leg, 384d MiniLM | `CODX_JUNIOR_DENSE_DIM` `:65` | ✅ | ✅ (IVF-PQ/HNSW) | ⚠️ brute force only |
| Sparse+dense fusion in one call | `AnnSearchRequest` + `RRFRanker`/`WeightedRanker` + `hybrid_search` `:1207-1223` | ✅ | ✅ `search(query_type="hybrid")` + RRF | ❌ write RRF yourself (~50 LOC) |
| Metadata filters (`source != ""`), JSON field | `NON_EMPTY_SOURCE_FILTER`, `FIELD_METADATA` | ✅ | ✅ `where=` | ⚠️ manual |
| Runs as its own service | `connect_milvus_client()` **at import** `:86` | required | none (embedded) | none (file) |

Verdict:

* **LanceDB ≈ equal (better for us)** for a single node up to millions of chunks:
  both search legs, RRF and filters exist natively, and it removes the container
  *and* the import-time connection (`:86`) that currently prevents the API from
  booting without Milvus. Different API, so it is an adapter, not a config flag.
* **sqlite-vec is lighter but not equal**: it is vector-only. BM25 would come from
  FTS5 (weaker code tokenizer) and the hybrid fusion is ours to write. Not worth it
  while lexical search is a core feature; it stays the "zero dependency" fallback.
* **Milvus stays** for the server tier (multi-project, big corpora, existing data).

Plan: `CODX_JUNIOR_KNOWLEDGE_BACKEND=lancedb|milvus`, default `lancedb` in tier 1/2,
`milvus` in the server profile. Cost: one adapter (`knowledge_lancedb.py`,
~700-900 LOC) behind the `KnowledgeDB` interface + tests; `knowledge_db` is imported
by 12 modules and `knowledge_milvus` by 24, so the interface must not change.
Embedding dimension must be stored per collection/index and a dim change must trigger
reindex (only the env var exists today).

### 6.2 Replace localai with provider key presets

Facts: there is **no `litellm` and no `anthropic` import** anywhere in `api/`; the
`OpenAISettings` / `AnthropicAISettings` / `MistralAISettings` classes in
`model/model.py:141-157` are vestigial. Everything goes through the `openai` client
(`openai>=2.24` in `pyproject.toml`) using `AIProvider(api_url, api_key)` +
`AIModel` entries of `GlobalSettings` (`model/model.py:305-325`), resolved by
`global_settings.get_provider_settings()`, which expands `$VAR` in `api_url`/`api_key`
(`global_settings.py:195`) — so secrets can stay in the environment.
The defaults (`model/ai_model.py:135-153`) point at `llmfactory`/Ollama env vars, i.e.
a fresh install has no usable model unless localai/ollama is running.

Proposal — first-run "connect a provider", one key, zero files:

* Presets are plain OpenAI-compatible base URLs, no new code path:
  `openai` `https://api.openai.com/v1`, `deepseek` `https://api.deepseek.com/v1`,
  `gemini` `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai`,
  plus openrouter/mistral/groq.
* `anthropic` has no OpenAI-compatible endpoint → only via the optional `litellm`
  proxy (`--profile anthropic`) or a dedicated adapter; keep it out of the trial default.
* On save: validate the key with `GET /models`, create the `AIProvider` + its `AIModel`s
  and fill the five global slots (`llm`, `rag`, `wiki`, `guardrail`, `embeddings`) plus
  `image_generation_model` / `image_vision_model` when the provider offers them.
* Embeddings must come from a provider when torch is absent (local MiniLM needs
  `sentence-transformers`, lazy-imported at `knowledge/embeddings.py:80-103`):
  `text-embedding-3-small` / `text-embedding-004`. Dim goes 384 → 1536 ⇒ reindex.
* `localai` remains as `--profile local-models`: the offline demo for people with no keys,
  just not started by default.

### 6.3 Keep a DEV deployment (all projects, watch, refresh)

Facts: DEBUG is not a profile today — the "production" compose already mounts the source
tree over the image (`- ../../.:/home/codx-junior/codx-junior` in the api *and* client
services, commented "Custom overrides (DEBUG)"), `run_api.sh` runs `uv sync` on every
start, and `run_client.sh` only runs `npm install && npm run dev` when `DEBUG` is set
(otherwise `npm run preview`). API reload is opt-in through `CODX_JUNIOR_API_RELOAD`
and intentionally not the default: every edit would restart uvicorn and interrupt the
in-flight agent turns.

Design — one compose base, additive overlays:

* **default (`prod`)**: pull-only image, source *not* mounted, no Node, no install on start.
* **`dev`** (`docker-compose.dev.yaml`): source mounted, `DEBUG=1`, Vite dev server with
  HMR (`server.watch` already ignores `**/.codx/**`), `CODX_JUNIOR_API_RELOAD=1` per
  service choice, `node_modules`/venv in named volumes (or a `dev` build target) so
  restarts never reinstall, several projects mounted at once (multi-project watch),
  `docker.sock` for workspaces.
* **`proxy`**, **`local-models`**, **`knowledge`** (milvus), **`anthropic`**: additive.

So the DEV stack keeps every project, watcher and hot reload, while the trial path
never pays for it.

---

## 7. What is implemented (demo tier)

Everything below is in the tree now; nothing here requires the user to build
anything.

### 7.1 New: `codx-junior-installer/demo/` — the trial deployment

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `demo/up.sh` | one command: validates the settings, creates `.env`, pulls (or `--build`s) the image, starts the stack, waits for health, applies the AI provider |
| `demo/docker-compose.yaml` | **one** service on port 19981 + optional `--profile knowledge` (Milvus). No Traefik, no LocalAI, no client container, no init containers, no `docker.sock` by default |
| `demo/Dockerfile` | two stages: `node:22-slim` compiles the SPA, `python:3.11-slim` runs it. No torch/vLLM/Playwright/TeX/Tesseract/Firefox, no Node at runtime |
| `demo/nginx.conf` | serves the built SPA and proxies `/api` (+ socket.io websocket) to `127.0.0.1:19980` — this is what removes Traefik and the second web server |
| `demo/supervisord.conf` | `api` + `api-background` + nginx in a single container (the two API containers of the old compose) |
| `demo/entrypoint.sh` | creates the folders, warns about missing settings, execs supervisord. **Installs nothing** |
| `demo/.env.example` | the whole settings surface, grouped required/optional |
| `demo/README.md` | the documentation: what you must pass, provider presets, what is auto-configured, what is left out, operations, troubleshooting |

### 7.2 Zero-touch AI configuration

* `api/codx/junior/bootstrap.py` (new) — provider presets (openai, deepseek,
  gemini, openrouter, mistral, groq, ollama, custom), builds the `AIProvider` +
  `AIModel` entries and fills the five global model slots. Idempotent (skips an
  already configured installation), non-destructive, offline, never fatal.
* `api/codx/junior/api/bootstrap.py` (new router, auto-discovered) —
  `GET /api/bootstrap` (state, dry run) and `POST /api/bootstrap/apply`
  (loopback only unless `CODX_JUNIOR_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOW_REMOTE=1`).
* `api/codx/junior/app.py` — calls the bootstrap on startup inside a try/except,
  so a broken environment cannot prevent the API from booting.

### 7.3 Build cost

* `.dockerignore` at the **repository root** (the build context is the repo root):
  excludes `node_modules`, `dist`, `.codx`, `.git`, `api/wiki`, `api/docs`,
  `design`, `docs`, `wiki`, tests and the installer-only assets. Markdown is *not*
  blanket-excluded because the runtime loads Markdown prompts.
* `api/pyproject.toml` — `torch`, `sentence-transformers`, `playwright` and
  `vllm` moved from `dependencies` to the extras `local-models`, `browser`,
  `vllm` and `full`. Verified: `torch` has **no** import in the code, `playwright`
  is referenced only by a test, `vllm_cpu_ai.py` is deprecated and
  `sentence_transformers` is already imported lazily with a friendly message.
* `scripts/install_api.sh` — installs `.[local-models,browser]` by default, so the
  full deployment keeps today's behaviour; a slim image passes
  `CODX_JUNIOR_API_EXTRAS=""`.
* `scripts/run_api.sh` — the recursive `chown` and `uv sync` now only run when
  `CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL != 1`. This was the 30 s+ cost of every container start.

### 7.4 Documentation

* `demo/README.md` — the settings reference (required vs optional, presets table,
  what codx-junior configures itself, what is left out, dev deployment,
  troubleshooting).
* `docs/getting-started.md` — the demo is now the first path; the full stack is
  described as the self-hosted deployment.

### 7.5 Still open (in the order I would do it)

1. Publish `codxjunior/codx-junior:demo` from CI so `demo/up.sh` is pull-only for
   real (`--build` exists as a fallback until then).
2. `knowledge_lancedb.py` adapter (§6.1) so the trial tier can have RAG without a

3. Embedding dimension stored in the index metadata (dim change ⇒ reindex) —

4. Image models (`image_generation_model` / `image_vision_model`) in the bootstrap
   presets, for the providers that support them.
5. Server tier: apply the same profile split (`proxy`, `local-models`, `knowledge`,
   `dev`) to `codx-junior/docker-compose.yaml`.

def docker_compose_build(service: Optional[str] = None, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Build docker-compose service images.

    Runs ``docker-compose build`` in the project directory, so a freshly created
    project gets its images built (something ``docker-compose start`` can never
    do). Base images are pulled automatically when missing.

    Args:
        service: Optional specific service name. If not provided, builds all services.
        **kwargs: Additional arguments including:
            - settings (CODXJuniorSettings): Project settings (required).
            - user (CodxUser): Current user (for audit logging).

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Build result with command output.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If service name contains invalid input.
        RuntimeError: If Docker Compose command fails.

    Example:
        >>> docker_compose_build()
        # Builds every service image
        >>> docker_compose_build("web")
        # Builds the web service image
    """
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings = kwargs.get("settings")
    user: CodxUser = kwargs.get("user")

    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    try:
        project_dir, compose_file, error = _compose_context(settings, "docker_compose_build")
        if error:
            return ToolResponse(user_response=f"❌ {error}", llm_response=error)

        if service:
            _validate_input(service, "service", allow_patterns=[r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-\.]+$"])

        command = _compose_base() + ["-f", compose_file, "build"]
        if service:
            command.append(service)

        operation = " ".join(command)
        result = _safe_exec_docker(command, timeout=900, cwd=project_dir)

        if not result.ok:
            logger.error("Docker Compose build error: %s", result.stderr)
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"❌ Build failed\n\n{_command_failure(operation, result)}",
                llm_response=(
                    f"`{operation}` failed with exit code {result.returncode}.\n"
                    f"stderr:\n{result.stderr.strip()}\nstdout:\n{result.stdout.strip()}"
                )
            )

        logger.info("Built compose %s by user %s", service or "all services",
                   user.username if user else "unknown")

        target = f"`{service}`" if service else "all services"
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=_format_command_feedback(operation, result.stdout),
            llm_response=f"Successfully built compose {target}.\nOutput:\n{result.stdout}"
        )

    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception("Error in docker_compose_build: %s", str(e))
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"❌ Error: {str(e)}",
            llm_response=f"Failed to build compose services: {str(e)}"
        )

"""
Zero-touch AI configuration ("first run bootstrap").

A demo/trial installation must be usable right after

    docker run ... -e CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY=... codxjunior/codx-junior:demo

Without this module that is not possible: a fresh installation has no usable
model, because the default :class:`GlobalSettings` points at the bundled
``llmfactory``/Ollama provider, which only exists when the ``local-models``
profile (LocalAI) is running.

This module reads provider settings from the environment, creates the
:class:`AIProvider` and its :class:`AIModel` entries and fills the five global
model slots (``llm``/``rag``/``wiki``/``guardrail``/``embeddings``).

Design rules
------------
* **Idempotent and non destructive.** It only runs when no provider other than
  the built-in ``llmfactory`` default has been configured, and never touches an
  installation that was already configured from the UI. ``CODX_JUNIOR_AI_FORCE=1``
  re-applies it (useful to rotate a key).
* **Offline.** No HTTP validation here: the container may start without network
  access. The UI validates the provider when a chat is sent, and
  ``POST /api/bootstrap/apply`` can be used to retry.
* **Never fatal.** Every error is logged; the API keeps booting.

CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER              openai | deepseek | gemini | openrouter |

"""
Bootstrap router – reports (and optionally re-applies) the zero-touch AI
configuration described in :mod:`codx.junior.bootstrap`.

Route layout
------------
GET  /api/bootstrap         – current configuration state (read only)
POST /api/bootstrap/apply   – re-apply the environment configuration

The ``apply`` endpoint is restricted to loopback clients (the container's own
``docker compose exec`` / health check) unless
``CODX_JUNIOR_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOW_REMOTE=1`` is set: it rewrites the global AI
settings, so it must not be reachable from the network by default.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import logging
import os

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Request

from codx.junior.bootstrap import bootstrap_ai_from_env

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

router = APIRouter(tags=["bootstrap"])

LOOPBACK_HOSTS = {"127.0.0.1", "::1", "localhost"}


def _is_allowed(request: Request) -> bool:
    """Allow the write endpoint from loopback (or explicitly from anywhere)."""
    if (os.environ.get("CODX_JUNIOR_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOW_REMOTE") or "").lower() in ("1", "true"):
        return True
    client = getattr(request, "client", None)
    return bool(client and client.host in LOOPBACK_HOSTS)


@router.get("/bootstrap")
def api_bootstrap_status() -> dict:
    """
    Report how the AI provider/models were configured.

    Dry run: nothing is written, so it is safe to call from the UI or from a
    deployment script that wants to know whether the instance is usable.
    """
    summary = bootstrap_ai_from_env(apply=False)
    return {"status": "ok", "bootstrap": summary}


@router.post("/bootstrap/apply")
def api_bootstrap_apply(request: Request) -> dict:
    """
    Re-apply the environment configuration (force).

    Used by the demo installer after the container is healthy, and by an admin
    who rotated an API key without recreating the volume.
    """
    if not _is_allowed(request):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Bootstrap can only be applied from localhost")

    summary = bootstrap_ai_from_env(force=True, apply=True)
    logger.info("Bootstrap apply requested: %s", summary.get("reason"))
    return {"status": "ok", "bootstrap": summary}

def _resolve_compose_file(project_dir: str, compose_file: str) -> "tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str]]":
    """
    Resolve an explicit compose file path, keeping it inside the project.

    A project can hold several stacks (for example ``docker-compose.yaml`` at the
    root plus ``codx-junior-installer/demo/docker-compose.yaml``). When the caller
    targets one of them explicitly, the path is resolved relative to the project
    directory and must stay inside it, so the tool can never read a compose file
    from an arbitrary location on the host.

    Args:
        project_dir: Absolute project directory.
        compose_file: Explicit compose file (relative to the project or absolute).

    Returns:
        Tuple ``(resolved_path, error)``; ``error`` is ``None`` on success.
    """
    candidate = compose_file.strip()
    if not candidate:
        return None, "compose_file is empty"
    if any(token in candidate for token in ("|", ";", "&", "`", "$", ">", "<")):
        return None, f"compose_file contains unsafe characters: {compose_file!r}"

    if not os.path.isabs(candidate):
        candidate = os.path.join(project_dir, candidate)
    candidate = os.path.realpath(candidate)
    root = os.path.realpath(project_dir)

    if os.path.commonpath([candidate, root]) != root:
        return None, f"compose_file must stay inside the project ({project_dir}): {compose_file!r}"
    if not os.path.isfile(candidate):
        return None, f"compose file not found: {compose_file!r}"
    if not candidate.endswith(COMPOSE_FILE_SUFFIXES):
        return None, (
            f"compose_file must end with {', '.join(COMPOSE_FILE_SUFFIXES)}: {compose_file!r}"
        )
    return candidate, None

    Compose profiles are how a stack ships optional services (the demo keeps
    Milvus in the ``knowledge`` profile), so the tools need to activate them.

    Args:
        profiles: Profile names to activate.

    Returns:
        List of command arguments (``["--profile", name, ...]``).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a profile name contains unsafe characters.
    """
    args: List[str] = []
    for profile in profiles or []:

        if not name:

    targets one of them explicitly, the path is resolved relative to the project
    directory and must stay inside it, so the tool can never read a compose file
    from an arbitrary location on the host.

    Args:
        project_dir: Absolute project directory.
        compose_file: Explicit compose file (relative to the project or absolute).

    Returns:
        Tuple ``(resolved_path, error)``; ``error`` is ``None`` on success.
    """
    candidate = compose_file.strip()
    if not candidate:
        return None, "compose_file is empty"
    if any(token in candidate for token in ("|", ";", "&", "`", "$", ">", "<")):
        return None, f"compose_file contains unsafe characters: {compose_file!r}"

    if not os.path.isabs(candidate):
        candidate = os.path.join(project_dir, candidate)
    candidate = os.path.realpath(candidate)
    root = os.path.realpath(project_dir)

    if os.path.commonpath([candidate, root]) != root:
        return None, f"compose_file must stay inside the project ({project_dir}): {compose_file!r}"
    if not os.path.isfile(candidate):
        return None, f"compose file not found: {compose_file!r}"
    if not candidate.endswith(COMPOSE_FILE_SUFFIXES):
        return None, (
            f"compose_file must end with {', '.join(COMPOSE_FILE_SUFFIXES)}: {compose_file!r}"
        )
    return candidate, None


def _compose_profile_args(profiles: Optional[List[str]]) -> List[str]:
    """
    Build the ``--profile`` arguments of a compose command.

    Compose profiles are how a stack ships optional services (the demo keeps
    Milvus in the ``knowledge`` profile), so the tools need to activate them.

    Args:
        profiles: Profile names to activate.

    Returns:
        List of command arguments (``["--profile", name, ...]``).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a profile name contains unsafe characters.
    """
    args: List[str] = []
    for profile in profiles or []:
        name = (profile or "").strip()
        if not name:
            continue
        if not re.match(r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-\.]+$", name):
            raise ValueError(f"invalid compose profile name: {profile!r}")
        args.extend(["--profile", name])
    return args


def _compose_context(
    settings: Optional[CODXJuniorSettings],
    tool_name: str,
    compose_file: Optional[str] = None,
) -> "tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str], Optional[str]]":
    """
    Resolve the project directory and compose file for a compose command.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.
        tool_name: Calling tool name (used in error messages).
        compose_file: Optional explicit compose file (relative to the project).
                      When omitted the first compose file found in the project
                      root or in the usual deployment sub directories is used.

    Returns:
        Tuple ``(project_dir, compose_file, error)``. ``error`` is ``None`` on
        success, otherwise a human-readable message explaining the failure.
    """
    project_dir = _project_cwd(settings)
    if not project_dir or not os.path.isdir(project_dir):
        return project_dir, None, (
            f"{tool_name}: no valid project directory (got {project_dir!r}). "
            "The Docker command must run from the project root."
        )
    if compose_file:
        resolved, error = _resolve_compose_file(project_dir, compose_file)
        if error:
            return project_dir, None, f"{tool_name}: {error}"
        return project_dir, resolved, None
    compose_file = _find_compose_file(project_dir)
    if not compose_file:
        return project_dir, None, (
            f"{tool_name}: no compose file found in {project_dir}. "
            f"Expected one of: {', '.join(COMPOSE_FILE_NAMES)}."
        )
    return project_dir, compose_file, None


def _compose_base() -> List[str]:
    """Return the base command for compose invocations."""
    override = os.environ.get(COMPOSE_CMD_ENV)
    if override:
        return shlex.split(override)
    return ["docker-compose"]


def _safe_exec_docker(command: List[str], timeout: int = 30, cwd: Optional[str] = None) -> DockerCommandResult:
    """
    Safely execute a Docker command using subprocess.

    Args:
        command: List of command arguments (no shell interpretation).
        timeout: Command timeout in seconds (default: 30).
        cwd: Working directory for the command. Compose needs the project root.

    Returns:
        DockerCommandResult: Captured stdout, stderr and exit code. Inspect
        ``result.ok`` (returncode == 0) to distinguish success from failure.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If the command times out or cannot be executed.
    """
    try:
        logger.debug("Executing Docker command: %s (cwd=%s)", " ".join(command), cwd)
        result = subprocess.run(
            command,
            cwd=cwd,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            text=True,
            timeout=timeout,
            check=False  # Don't raise on non-zero exit
        )

        stdout = result.stdout or ""
        stderr = result.stderr or ""
        if result.returncode != 0:
            logger.warning(
                "Docker command failed with exit code %d: %s\nstderr: %s",
                result.returncode, " ".join(command), stderr
            )
        else:
            logger.debug("Docker command succeeded: %s", " ".join(command))
        return DockerCommandResult(stdout=stdout, stderr=stderr, returncode=result.returncode)

    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        logger.error("Docker command timeout: %s", " ".join(command))
        raise RuntimeError(f"Command timed out after {timeout}s") from e
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        binary = command[0] if command else "docker"
        logger.error("Docker command not found: %s", binary)
        raise RuntimeError(f"Docker command not found: {binary}") from e
    except Exception as e:
        error_msg = str(e)
        logger.error("Error executing Docker command: %s", error_msg)
        raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to execute Docker command: {error_msg}") from e


def _format_command_feedback(operation: str, output: str, empty_text: str = "_(no output)_") -> str:
    """
    Build user-facing feedback that always shows the executed Docker operation
    together with its output, so the chat never displays an empty result.

    Args:
        operation: Human-readable description of the Docker command executed
                   (e.g. "docker-compose run --rm api").
        output: Captured command output (stdout). May be empty.
        empty_text: Placeholder shown when there is no output.

    Returns:
        str: Markdown block using the format::

            > Running: `<operation>`
            Output:

            <output or empty_text>
    """
    output = (output or "").strip()
    if not output:
        output = empty_text
    return f"> Running: `{operation}`\nOutput:\n\n{output}"


def _command_failure(operation: str, result: DockerCommandResult) -> str:
    """
    Build a failure block showing the command, both streams and exit code.

    Args:
        operation: Human-readable command string that was executed.
        result: The failed command result.

    Returns:
        str: Markdown block with the command, exit code and any captured output.
    """
    parts = [f"> Running: `{operation}`", f"Exit code: {result.returncode}"]
    if result.stderr.strip():
        parts.append(f"stderr:\n{result.stderr.strip()}")
    if result.stdout.strip():
        parts.append(f"stdout:\n{result.stdout.strip()}")
    return "\n\n".join(parts)


def _create_or_run_container(
    mode: str,
    image: str,
    container_name: str,
    detach: bool,
    port_mapping: Optional[str],
    env_vars: Optional[Dict[str, str]],
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings,
    user: Optional[CodxUser],
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Shared implementation for ``docker run`` and ``docker create``.

    Args:
        mode: Either ``"run"`` or ``"create"``.
        image: Docker image name/ID.
        container_name: Name for the container.
        detach: Run in background (only meaningful for ``run``).
        port_mapping: Optional ``host:container`` port mapping.
        env_vars: Optional environment variables.
        settings: Project settings.
        user: Current user (audit logging).

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Container creation/start result.
    """
    _validate_input(container_name, "container_name", allow_patterns=[r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-\.]+$"])
    _validate_input(image, "image", allow_patterns=[r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-\.:/@]+$"])
    project_dir = _project_cwd(settings)

    command = ["docker", mode]
    if mode == "run":
        command.append("-d" if detach else "-it")
    command.extend(["--name", container_name])

    if port_mapping:
        _validate_input(port_mapping, "port_mapping", allow_patterns=[r"^\d+:\d+$"])
        command.extend(["-p", port_mapping])

    for key, value in (env_vars or {}).items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not isinstance(value, str):
            raise ValueError("Environment variables must be strings")
        _validate_input(key, f"env_var_key_{key}")
        _validate_input(value, f"env_var_value_{key}")
        command.extend(["-e", f"{key}={value}"])

    command.append(image)
    operation = " ".join(command)

    result = _safe_exec_docker(command, timeout=120, cwd=project_dir)

    if not result.ok:
        logger.error(
            "Docker %s failed for user %s: %s",
            mode, user.username if user else "unknown", result.stderr
        )
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"❌ Failed to {mode} container `{container_name}`\n\n"
                          f"{_command_failure(operation, result)}",
            llm_response=(
                f"`{operation}` failed with exit code {result.returncode}.\n"
                f"stderr: {result.stderr.strip()}\nstdout: {result.stdout.strip()}"
            )
        )

    container_id = "unknown"
    if result.stdout.strip():
        container_id = result.stdout.strip().splitlines()[0][:12]

    verb = "created" if mode == "create" else "started"
    logger.info(
        "Docker %s container %s (image=%s) for user %s",
        mode, container_name, image, user.username if user else "unknown"
    )

    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=_format_command_feedback(
            operation,
            f"Container `{container_name}` {verb} successfully (ID: `{container_id}`)"
        ),
        llm_response=(
            f"Successfully {verb} container {container_name} from image {image} "
            f"(ID: {container_id})."
        )
    )


def docker_ps(filters: Optional[str] = None, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    List Docker containers.

    Lists all running and stopped containers, optionally filtered by status or labels.
    Includes the image, status/health, ports and the compose project/service labels
    so a compose stack can be verified without follow-up ``inspect`` calls.

    Args:
        filters: Optional Docker filter (e.g., "status=running", "label=project=myapp").
                 Must not contain unsafe characters.
        **kwargs: Additional arguments including:
            - settings (CODXJuniorSettings): Project settings (required).
            - user (CodxUser): Current user (for audit logging).

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Container listing with detailed information.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If filters contain unsafe input.
        RuntimeError: If Docker command fails.

    Example:
        >>> docker_ps(filters="status=running")
        # Lists all running containers
    """
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings = kwargs.get("settings")
    user: CodxUser = kwargs.get("user")

    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    try:
        ps_format = "\t".join([
            "{{.ID}}",
            "{{.Names}}",
            "{{.Image}}",
            "{{.Status}}",
            "{{.Ports}}",
            '{{.Label "com.docker.compose.project"}}',
            '{{.Label "com.docker.compose.service"}}',
        ])
        command = ["docker", "ps", "-a", "--format", ps_format]

        if filters:
            _validate_input(filters, "filters", allow_patterns=[r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-\.=]+$"])
            command.extend(["--filter", filters])

        operation = " ".join(command)
        result = _safe_exec_docker(command, cwd=_project_cwd(settings))

        if not result.ok:
            logger.error("Docker ps error for user %s: %s", user.username if user else "unknown", result.stderr)
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"❌ Failed to list containers\n\n{_command_failure(operation, result)}",
                llm_response=f"Error listing containers (exit {result.returncode}): {result.stderr.strip()}"
            )

        if not result.stdout.strip():
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response="✓ No containers found",
                llm_response="No containers currently running"
            )

        # Parse and format output
        lines = [line for line in result.stdout.strip().split('\n') if line.strip()]
        formatted_lines = [
            "**Container ID** | **Name** | **Image** | **Status** | **Ports** | "
            "**Compose Project** | **Compose Service**"
        ]
        formatted_lines.append("---|---|---|---|---|---|---")
        for line in lines:
            parts = line.split('\t')
            if len(parts) >= 3:
                container_id = parts[0]
                container_name = parts[1]
                image = parts[2] if len(parts) > 2 else "-"
                status = parts[3] if len(parts) > 3 else "unknown"
                ports = parts[4] if len(parts) > 4 and parts[4] else "-"
                project = parts[5] if len(parts) > 5 and parts[5] else "-"
                service = parts[6] if len(parts) > 6 and parts[6] else "-"
                formatted_lines.append(
                    f"`{container_id[:12]}` | `{container_name}` | `{image}` | {status} | "
                    f"{ports} | {project} | {service}"
                )

        logger.info("Listed %d containers for user %s", len(lines), user.username if user else "unknown")

        user_response = _format_command_feedback(operation, "\n".join(formatted_lines))
        # llm_response is the ONLY content the model receives (user_response is
        # shown in the chat but not sent to the model). Include the real data and
        # echo the exact command so filtered listings are not mislabeled.
        llm_response = (
            f"Found {len(lines)} container(s). Command: `{operation}`\n"
            f"Raw output (ID\tName\tImage\tStatus\tPorts\tProject\tService):\n"
            f"{result.stdout.strip()}"
        )
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=user_response,
            llm_response=llm_response
        )

    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception("Error in docker_ps: %s", str(e))
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"❌ Error: {str(e)}",
            llm_response=f"Failed to list containers: {str(e)}"
        )


def docker_logs(container_name: str, tail: int = 100, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Retrieve Docker container logs.

    Fetches the last N lines of logs from a container.

    Args:
        container_name: Name or ID of the container.
        tail: Number of log lines to retrieve (1-1000, default: 100).
        **kwargs: Additional arguments including:
            - settings (CODXJuniorSettings): Project settings (required).
            - user (CodxUser): Current user (for audit logging).

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Container logs formatted for display.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If container_name or tail contain invalid input.
        RuntimeError: If Docker command fails.

    Example:
        >>> docker_logs("myapp_container", tail=50)
        # Shows last 50 lines of container logs
    """
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings = kwargs.get("settings")
    user: CodxUser = kwargs.get("user")

    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    try:
        # Validate inputs
        _validate_input(container_name, "container_name", allow_patterns=[r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-\.]+$"])

        if not isinstance(tail, int) or tail < 1 or tail > 1000:
            raise ValueError("tail must be integer between 1-1000")

        command = ["docker", "logs", "--tail", str(tail), container_name]
        operation = " ".join(command)
        result = _safe_exec_docker(command, timeout=10, cwd=_project_cwd(settings))

        if not result.ok:
            logger.error("Docker logs error for container %s: %s", container_name, result.stderr)
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"❌ Failed to retrieve logs\n\n{_command_failure(operation, result)}",
                llm_response=(
                    f"Error retrieving logs for {container_name} "
                    f"(exit {result.returncode}): {result.stderr.strip()}"
                )
            )

        # docker logs sends the container's stderr stream to our stderr, so a
        # successful command may still carry content there. Include both.
        output = (result.stdout or "") + (result.stderr or "")
        if not output.strip():
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"✓ No logs available for `{container_name}`",
                llm_response="Container has no log entries"
            )

        logger.info("Retrieved logs for container %s (tail=%d) by user %s",
                   container_name, tail, user.username if user else "unknown")

        user_response = _format_command_feedback(operation, output)
        # Provide the actual log content to the model (not just a summary).
        llm_response = (
            f"Logs for container '{container_name}' (last {tail} lines):\n{output}"
        )
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=user_response,
            llm_response=llm_response
        )

    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception("Error in docker_logs: %s", str(e))
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"❌ Error: {str(e)}",
            llm_response=f"Failed to retrieve logs: {str(e)}"
        )


def docker_stats(container_name: Optional[str] = None, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Show Docker container resource statistics.

    Displays CPU, memory, network I/O, and block I/O statistics for one or all containers.
    Useful for performance monitoring and debugging.

    Args:
        container_name: Optional specific container name. If not provided, shows all containers.
        **kwargs: Additional arguments including:
            - settings (CODXJuniorSettings): Project settings (required).
            - user (CodxUser): Current user (for audit logging).

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Container statistics formatted for display.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If container_name contains invalid input.
        RuntimeError: If Docker command fails.

    Example:
        >>> docker_stats()
        # Shows stats for all containers
        >>> docker_stats("myapp_container")
        # Shows stats for specific container
    """
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings = kwargs.get("settings")
    user: CodxUser = kwargs.get("user")

    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    try:
        if container_name:
            _validate_input(container_name, "container_name", allow_patterns=[r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-\.]+$"])
            command = ["docker", "stats", "--no-stream", container_name]
        else:
            command = ["docker", "stats", "--no-stream"]

        operation = " ".join(command)
        result = _safe_exec_docker(command, timeout=15, cwd=_project_cwd(settings))

        if not result.ok:
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"❌ Failed to retrieve statistics\n\n{_command_failure(operation, result)}",
                llm_response=f"Error retrieving container stats (exit {result.returncode}): {result.stderr.strip()}"
            )

        if not result.stdout.strip():
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response="✓ No statistics available",
                llm_response="No running containers to show statistics for"
            )

        logger.info("Retrieved stats for %s by user %s",
                   container_name or "all containers", user.username if user else "unknown")

        user_response = _format_command_feedback(operation, result.stdout)
        # Provide the actual statistics to the model (not just a summary).
        llm_response = (
            f"Container statistics for {container_name or 'all containers'}:\n{result.stdout}"

        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=user_response,
            llm_response=llm_response
        )

    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception("Error in docker_stats: %s", str(e))
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"❌ Error: {str(e)}",
            llm_response=f"Failed to retrieve statistics: {str(e)}"
        )

def docker_images(**kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    List available Docker images.

    Shows all locally available Docker images with repository, tag, ID, size,
    and creation date. Useful for managing project dependencies.

    Args:
        **kwargs: Additional arguments including:
            - settings (CODXJuniorSettings): Project settings (required).
            - user (CodxUser): Current user (for audit logging).

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Image listing with detailed information.

    Example:
        >>> docker_images()
        # Lists all available Docker images
    """

    user: CodxUser = kwargs.get("user")

    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    try:
        command = ["docker", "images", "--format", "{{.Repository}}\t{{.Tag}}\t{{.ID}}\t{{.Size}}\t{{.CreatedAt}}"]
        operation = " ".join(command)
        result = _safe_exec_docker(command, cwd=_project_cwd(settings))

        if not result.ok:

                user_response=f"❌ Failed to list images\n\n{_command_failure(operation, result)}",
                llm_response=f"Error listing Docker images (exit {result.returncode}): {result.stderr.strip()}"

        if not result.stdout.strip():
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response="✓ No Docker images found",

        logger.info("Listed Docker images for user %s: %d images", user.username if user else "unknown", len(lines))

        user_response = _format_command_feedback(operation, "\n".join(formatted_lines))

def docker_run(image: str, container_name: str, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Run a Docker container from an image.

    Creates and starts a new container with specified configuration and security
    constraints. ``docker run`` pulls the image automatically when it is not cached
    locally, so it can also be used to obtain an image.

    Args:
        image: Docker image name/ID to run.
        container_name: Name for the new container.
        **kwargs: Additional arguments including:
            - settings (CODXJuniorSettings): Project settings (required).
            - user (CodxUser): Current user (for audit logging).
            - detach (bool): Run in background (default: True).
            - port_mapping (str): Port mapping (e.g., "8080:80").
            - env_vars (dict): Environment variables.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Container creation confirmation with container ID.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If inputs contain invalid values or unsafe patterns.
        RuntimeError: If Docker command fails.

    Example:
        >>> docker_run("nginx:latest", "myapp_web_1", port_mapping="8080:80")
        # Runs nginx container
    """

def docker_exec(
    container_name: str,
    command: str,
    timeout: int = 60,
    **kwargs,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Run one command inside a running container (``docker exec``).

    This is the runtime feedback loop that was missing: it makes the *loaded*
    code observable instead of guessed from logs, e.g.

        docker_exec(
            "codx-junior-api",
            "grep -n estimation_cost /app/codx/junior/task_manager.py",
        )

    The command is split with :func:`shlex.split` and executed **without a
    shell**, so pipes, redirections and substitutions are rejected with an
    explicit message (issue one command per call). Destructive first tokens
    (``rm``, ``dd``, ``kill`` ...) are refused.

    Args:
        container_name: Running container (letters, digits, ``_ - .``).
        command: Command line to execute inside the container.
        timeout: Seconds before the command is killed (1-300, default: 60).
        **kwargs: Additional arguments including:
            - settings (CODXJuniorSettings): Project settings (required).
            - user (CodxUser): Current user (for audit logging).

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Captured stdout/stderr plus the exit code. A non-zero
        exit is reported as a failure, never as a success.
    """
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings = kwargs.get("settings")
    user: CodxUser = kwargs.get("user")

    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    try:
        _validate_input(container_name, "container_name", allow_patterns=[r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-\.]+$"])

        if not isinstance(timeout, int) or timeout < 1 or timeout > 300:
            raise ValueError("timeout must be integer between 1-300 seconds")

        raw_command = (command or "").strip()
        if not raw_command:
            raise ValueError("command is required")
        if len(raw_command) > 1000:
            raise ValueError("command must be at most 1000 characters")
        for token in DOCKER_EXEC_SHELL_CHARS:
            if token in raw_command:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"command must not contain '{token}': docker exec runs without a "
                    "shell, so issue one command per call"
                )

        argv = shlex.split(raw_command)
        if not argv:
            raise ValueError("command is required")
        program = os.path.basename(argv[0])
        if program in DOCKER_EXEC_DENIED_COMMANDS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"command '{program}' is not allowed in docker exec: use a targeted, "
                "non-destructive diagnostic command"
            )

        docker_command = ["docker", "exec", container_name] + argv
        operation = " ".join(docker_command)
        result = _safe_exec_docker(
            docker_command, timeout=timeout, cwd=_project_cwd(settings)
        )

        output = result.stdout or ""
        if (result.stderr or "").strip():
            output = f"{output}\n{result.stderr}" if output.strip() else result.stderr

        logger.info(
            "Docker exec in %s by user %s: %s (exit=%s)",
            container_name,
            user.username if user else "unknown",
            raw_command,
            result.returncode,
        )

        if not result.ok:
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"❌ Command failed\n\n{_command_failure(operation, result)}",
                llm_response=(
                    f"docker exec failed (exit {result.returncode}) in {container_name}:\n"
                    f"{(output or '').strip()[:4000] or '_(no output)_'}"
                )
            )

        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=_format_command_feedback(operation, (output or "").strip()),
            llm_response=(
                f"docker exec in {container_name} (exit 0):\n"
                f"{(output or '').strip()[:4000] or '_(no output)_'}"
            )
        )

    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception("Error in docker_exec: %s", str(e))
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"❌ Error: {str(e)}",
            llm_response=f"Failed to exec in container {container_name}: {str(e)}"
        )


def docker_compose_run(service: str, command: Optional[str] = None, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Run a one-off command in a docker-compose service.

    Executes a command in a service defined in the project's compose file. The
    command string is split into arguments (no shell interpretation) and the
    command runs from the project directory, using the project's compose file.

    Args:
        service: Service name in the compose file.
        command: Optional command to execute in the service (e.g. "curl http://domain.com/path?param=value").
        **kwargs: Additional arguments including:
            - settings (CODXJuniorSettings): Project settings (required).
            - user (CodxUser): Current user (for audit logging).
            - no_deps (bool): Do not start linked services (default: False).

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Command execution result.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If inputs contain invalid values.
        RuntimeError: If Docker Compose command fails.

    Example:
        >>> docker_compose_run("web", "python manage.py migrate")
        # Runs migration in web service
        >>> docker_compose_run("web", "curl http://domain.com/api?key=12345")
        # Executes curl with URL parameters
    """
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings = kwargs.get("settings")
    user: CodxUser = kwargs.get("user")
    no_deps = kwargs.get("no_deps", False)

    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    try:
        project_dir, compose_file, error = _compose_context(settings, "docker_compose_run")
        if error:
            return ToolResponse(user_response=f"❌ {error}", llm_response=error)

        _validate_input(service, "service", allow_patterns=[r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-\.]+$"])
        if command:
            _validate_input(command, "command", allow_patterns=COMMAND_EXECUTION_ALLOWED_CHARS)

        compose_command = _compose_base() + ["-f", compose_file, "run", "--rm"]
        if no_deps:
            compose_command.append("--no-deps")
        compose_command.append(service)
        if command:
            compose_command.extend(shlex.split(command))

        operation = " ".join(compose_command)
        result = _safe_exec_docker(compose_command, timeout=60, cwd=project_dir)

        if not result.ok:
            logger.error("Docker Compose run error for service %s: %s", service, result.stderr)
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"❌ Failed to run service `{service}`\n\n{_command_failure(operation, result)}",
                llm_response=f"Error running compose service {service}: {result.stderr.strip()}"
            )

        logger.info("Executed compose run on service %s by user %s", service,
                   user.username if user else "unknown")

        # Always show the executed command and its output (placeholder when empty),
        # so the user never sees an empty result.
        user_response = _format_command_feedback(operation, result.stdout)
        # Provide the command output to the model (not just a status summary).
        llm_response = (
            f"Command executed on '{service}' service"
            + (f" (command: {command})" if command else "")
            + f". Output:\n{result.stdout}"
        )
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=user_response,
            llm_response=llm_response
        )

    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception("Error in docker_compose_run: %s", str(e))
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"❌ Error: {str(e)}",
            llm_response=f"Failed to run compose service: {str(e)}"
        )

        RuntimeError: If Docker Compose command fails.

    Example:
        >>> docker_compose_build()
        # Builds every service image
        >>> docker_compose_build("web")
        # Builds the web service image
    """
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings = kwargs.get("settings")
    user: CodxUser = kwargs.get("user")

    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    try:
        project_dir, compose_file, error = _compose_context(settings, "docker_compose_build")
        if error:
            return ToolResponse(user_response=f"❌ {error}", llm_response=error)

        if service:

        if service:

        result = _safe_exec_docker(command, timeout=900, cwd=project_dir)

        if not result.ok:
            logger.error("Docker Compose build error: %s", result.stderr)

                user_response=f"❌ Build failed\n\n{_command_failure(operation, result)}",
                llm_response=(

            llm_response=f"Successfully built compose {target}.\nOutput:\n{result.stdout}"
